extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians working on Inter-universal Teichmüller theory, arithmetic geometry, and Frobenioids
extracted.subtask_description: Developing group-theoretic algorithms for the Hodge–Arakelov-theoretic evaluation of étale theta functions on l-torsion points and relating these constructions to (tempered) Frobenioids; includes notions like conjugate synchronization, cyclotomic rigidity, theta monoids, and their functoriality and splittings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugate synchronization
rubrics_metrics.description: The evaluation algorithm is performed relative to a single basepoint; the collection of theta values (for various |t| ∈ |Fl|) are all computed relative to a single copy of the Galois group Gv(Π_v¨) and a single cyclotome (l·ΔΘ)(Π_v¨).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the collection of theta values as one unified entity so that Kummer theory may be performed by considering the action of a single Galois group on simultaneous extraction of N-th roots of all theta values, relative to a single cyclotome compatible with the base-field Kummer theory. This single-basepoint phenomenon is necessary for performing Kummer theory and is referred to as conjugate synchronization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single basepoint requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose a single basepoint of a suitable category of coverings of a geometric object consisting of a single connected component to realize conjugate synchronization and related constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The single basepoint underlies both conjugate synchronization and label synchronization; it gives rise to topological groups Π_v, (Δ±)Π_v, etc., which must be viewed as originating from that single basepoint for compatibility of subsequent constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with F^±_l-symmetry vs F_l-symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Conjugate synchronization basepoint is compatible with the F^±_l-symmetry of [IUTchI], §6, but may be incompatible with the F_l-symmetry in the case of certain D-ΘNF-Hodge theaters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the F^±_l-symmetry (defined relative to a single copy of a local geometric object) when label-synchronization and comparison with label zero and O× splittings are required; be aware that F_l-symmetry involves permuting multiple copies and can produce label crushing and incompatibility with single-basepoint conjugate synchronization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connectedness of admissible subgraph Γ' ⊆ Γ¨Y
rubrics_metrics.description: Any subgraph Γ' used for restricting the theory must be connected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connectedness is essential (cf. use of archimedean line segment Γ_X ⊆ ΓX) for the constructions and for the discrete/cyclotomic rigidity arguments; non-connected subgraphs are not acceptable for the single-basepoint/conjugate-synchronization viewpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Containment of the vertex labeled 0 in Γ'
rubrics_metrics.description: For the crucial splittings of Corollary 2.6 and related constructions, the chosen subgraph Γ' must contain the vertex of Γ¨Y labeled '0'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement (together with connectedness) imposes severe restrictions on Γ' and the collection of étale theta values obtainable by restriction to μ−-translates of cusps lying in Γ'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and maximization of ||Γ'||
rubrics_metrics.description: For finite Γ', define ||Γ'|| := |Γ'|^{-1} · sum_{j in image} min_{j in fiber} {j^2} (with conventions); as a function of |Γ'|, ||Γ'|| is monotone increasing and attains the maximum when |Γ'| = l and is constant for |Γ'| ≥ l.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the viewpoint of height inequalities and global considerations, maximize ||Γ'||; formally this leads to taking Γ' = Γ¨Y (no loss of generality) when optimizing this quantity under given constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product-formula compatibility (globalization constraint)
rubrics_metrics.description: When globalizing via realified Frobenioids in §4, impose the product formula; fibers of Γ' over |Fl| containing more than one element produce indeterminacies incompatible with the product formula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To globalize compatibly with the product formula and to maximize ||Γ'||, the only compatible choice for Γ' is Γ¨Y; this avoids the conjugacy indeterminacies that would otherwise violate the product formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use isomorphisms (l·ΔΘ)(−) ∼→ Π_μ(−) (or μ_Z(G_v(−)) in base-field-theoretic formulation) to replace cyclotome-structures by explicit cyclotomic modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply cyclotomic rigidity to translate '(l·ΔΘ)(−)' into Π_μ(−) (multiradial formulation) or μ_Z(G_v(−)) (uniradial base-field-theoretic formulation); these isomorphisms are crucial for obtaining splittings at zero-labeled evaluation points and for relating group-theoretic theta evaluation to Frobenioid-theoretic structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction of étale theta functions to subgraphs and evaluation points
rubrics_metrics.description: The cyclotomic-rigidity-replaced subsets θ_ι, ∞θ_ι, θ_t_env, ∞θ_t_env etc., are constructed as ι_γ-invariant subsets in direct limits of H^1; upon restriction to decomposition groups they yield μ^{2l}- and μ-orbits indexed by labels |t| ∈ |Fl|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When forming these subsets, use the cyclotomic-rigidity isomorphisms to replace (l·ΔΘ)(−) by Π_μ(−) or μ_Z(G_v(−)); the resulting θ_|t| depend only on the label |t| and are functorial in the projective system of mono-theta environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial group-theoretic evaluation algorithm
rubrics_metrics.description: An algorithm that, starting from arbitrary Δ^±_v- or Π^±_v-conjugates and ranging over LabCusp^±(Π_γ_v), constructs collections of μ^{2l}- and μ-orbits {θ_|t|_env((MΘ_∗)^{γ})}|t|∈|Fl| and corresponding infinite-orbit sets, functorial in the projective system MΘ_∗ and compatible with independent conjugacy actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This group-theoretic construction yields the evaluation data and is compatible with conjugation actions by Δ^±_v and Π^±_v; it can be applied in both the mono-theta-theoretic and base-field-theoretic frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Splittings at zero-labeled evaluation points
rubrics_metrics.description: When the evaluation point t is zero, applying cyclotomic rigidity to replace (l·ΔΘ)(−) by Π_μ(−) yields splittings (up to torsion) of monoids of the form M ×_{TM} ... compatible with Corollary 1.12, (ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the second restriction operation to obtain explicit splittings at zero-labeled points; these splittings are compatible (relative to the first restriction) with previous splittings and are important structural outputs of the evaluation algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradial vs uniradial formulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Cyclotomes Π_μ(−) admit a multiradial formulation, while μ_Z(G_v(−)) (base-field-theoretic cyclotomes) admit only a uniradial formulation unless one sacrifices cyclotomic rigidity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithms in the base-field-theoretic (μ_Z) viewpoint produce only uniradial functors; however, by applying log-shell theory (later chapters), one may modify algorithms to become manifestly multiradial at the cost of mild indeterminacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theta monoids (split theta monoids)
rubrics_metrics.description: From the direct limit of cohomology modules and the constructed subsets M ×_{TM}·θ_ι, one constructs submonoids Ψ_ι_env(MΘ_∗) (theta monoids) and their infinite analogues ∞Ψ_ι_env(MΘ_∗); these come equipped with natural conjugation actions and splittings up to torsion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a functorial algorithm producing the collection Ψ_env(MΘ_∗) = {Ψ_ι_env(MΘ_∗)}_ι and ∞Ψ_env, each being the submonoid generated by the indicated subsets; think of each Ψ_ι_env as a theta monoid with the indicated structural properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant monoids
rubrics_metrics.description: By applying cyclotomic rigidity and considering inverse images of Z inside μ_Z(G_v(−)), one obtains a monoid of constants Ψ_cns(MΘ_∗) = MTM(MΘ_∗) ⊆ direct limit H^1, naturally isomorphic to O_{F_v} (or the indicated constant monoid) with a conjugation action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This constant monoid is constructed functorially and plays the role of constants in the theta-monoid setting; compatibility with conjugation by Π_X(MΘ_∗) is part of the construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruction of theta-data from tempered Frobenioids
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a tempered Frobenioid F_v (or a Θ-Hodge theater †F_v), one can reconstruct category-theoretically the collections of submonoids Ψ^{FΘ}_v, ∞Ψ^{FΘ}_v and Ψ^{Cv} (up to inner automorphism indeterminacy) associated to characteristic pro-objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the category-theoretic constructions (evaluating O(−) on characteristic pro-objects A^Θ_∞) to obtain the monoids with conjugation actions; note that the reconstruction is well-defined up to inner automorphisms of Π_v.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formation of Kummer classes and compatibility with Frobenioid structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Form Kummer classes by extracting N-th roots of unity (N ≥ 1) relative to the Frobenioid structure; these yield isomorphisms Ψ^{†FΘ}_{v,α} ≅ Ψ_ι_env(MΘ_∗) (and for infinite analogues) that are well-defined up to inner automorphisms and compatible with conjugation actions and splittings up to torsion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the description of exterior cyclotome from Proposition 1.3 and the Kummer-class construction to relate Frobenioid-theoretic theta monoids to the env-theory; these identifications respect Π-actions and the torsion splittings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functoriality and compatibility under poly-isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: A full poly-isomorphism MΘ_∗(Π_v) ∼→ MΘ_∗(†F_v) induces compatible isomorphisms of the associated topological groups, monoids (Ψ_env, ∞Ψ_env), and G_v-objects, preserving Π-actions and splittings (up to torsion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composing the algorithms of Propositions 1.2 and 3.1, ensure compatibility with arbitrary automorphisms of the ind-topological monoid equipped with its Π-action; the displayed diagrams in Proposition 3.4 encode these compatibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of archimedean line segment (Γ_X ⊆ ΓX) and discrete rigidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Selecting the archimedean line segment Γ_X ⊆ ΓX singles out elements with absolute value ≤ l within nonarchimedean congruence classes, relying essentially on the discreteness of Z (discrete rigidity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This argument is analogous to computing global sections of arithmetic line bundles and is dual to cyclotomic rigidity; connectedness of the archimedean segment is essential for these discrete-rigidity arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent conjugacy indeterminacies and fiber constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent conjugacy indeterminacies imply that one cannot restrict the étale theta function to a single j ∈ Γ' without simultaneously restricting to all j in the same fiber over |Fl|; fibers with multiple elements create indeterminacies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for these indeterminacies when choosing subgraphs and when attempting local-to-global constructions; they motivate the restriction to Γ¨Y under globalization and product-formula constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of monoids and splittings up to torsion
rubrics_metrics.description: All constructed monoids (theta monoids, constant monoids, Frobenioid-theoretic monoids) come equipped with characteristic splittings up to torsion which are compatible with Π-actions and conjugation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing or comparing monoids, always record the splittings up to torsion and verify compatibility with conjugation actions and the cyclotomic-rigidity identifications; splittings are essential for rigidity and comparison arguments.
